todo.description: A beloved local bookshop acting as a cultural anchor for the neighborhood's bustling literary and arts scene.
todo.action: Browse the quirky, hand-curated stacks and support local booksellers.

todo.title: Peckham Levels & Frank's Cafe
todo.description: Peckham pioneered repurposing brutalist multi-storey car parks into community art spaces and rooftop bars.
todo.action: Take the stairs to the roof of Frank's Cafe for sunset skyline views.
todo.photoTip: Frank's Cafe / Peckham Levels: Pink staircases and unobstructed skyline views.

todo.title: Peckham Rye Park & Sexby Garden
todo.description: A 113-acre historic common and ornamental park featuring a restored Victorian sunken garden and ancient arboretum.
todo.action: Walk through the wisteria pergola in the Sexby Garden and stroll along the River Peck.
todo.photoTip: The blooming wisteria pergola and ornamental fountain in the Sexby Garden.

moreTodo.title: Asylum Chapel (Caroline Gardens)
moreTodo.booking: Check open days or special exhibitions online
moreTodo.description: A bombed-out 1826 Georgian chapel left in a romantic state of ruined decay with distressed stone walls and stained glass.
moreTodo.action: Admire the Doric portico and evocative weathered interior walls during public art shows.
moreTodo.photoTip: Sunlight streaming through distressed stained-glass windows onto textured crumbling plaster walls.

moreTodo.title: Bussey Building & Copeland Park
moreTodo.booking: No booking required / Event tickets vary
moreTodo.description: A sprawling former cricket bat factory saved from demolition, now a buzzing 5-acre creative compound of artist studios and vintage pop-ups.
moreTodo.action: Explore the vintage arcades and grab an artisan coffee in the courtyard.
moreTodo.photoTip: Industrial red-brick factory chimneys and bold street art murals in the alleyways.

eat.title: Forza Wine Peckham
eat.description: Trendy Italian rooftop wine bar overlooking the South London skyline.
eat.mustTry: Fantastic vegetarian small plates with great gluten-free adaptations.

eat.title: Levan
eat.description: Stylish contemporary European restaurant inspired by Parisian bistros.
eat.mustTry: Creative vegetarian seasonal dishes with excellent gluten-free support.

name: Dulwich & Crystal Palace 🦕
durationReason: Dulwich Picture Gallery and the vast Horniman Museum take hours on their own; exploring the Crystal Palace dinosaurs and vintage Triangle is best enjoyed on a dedicated second day.
season: October. Ancient woods and leafy village streets turn gold and red like a countryside retreat.
transport: 🚇 Overground to Crystal Palace, or Southeastern rail to North Dulwich.
funFacts: Dulwich Picture Gallery was designed by Sir John Soane and is the world's first purpose-built public art gallery.
The Crystal Palace dinosaurs were built in 1854 and represent the first ever attempt to sculpt life-size extinct animals.
Dulwich remains so unspoiled because much of it is owned by a single historic charity estate from the 1600s.
soul: Deep South London elegance. Dulwich is a pristine affluent village; Crystal Palace is bohemian with a massive Victorian park.

todo.title: Dulwich Picture Gallery
todo.description: Designed by Sir John Soane in 1811, this is the world's first purpose-built public art gallery, bathed in natural top-lighting.
todo.action: Visit the gallery to see masterpieces by Rembrandt, Rubens, and Canaletto.
todo.photoTip: Exterior brickwork and lighting enfilades of the Dulwich Picture Gallery.

todo.title: Crystal Palace Antiques Market
todo.description: The Crystal Palace 'Triangle' is renowned for its bohemian, eccentric collection of vintage and antique stores.
todo.action: Hunt through the multi-level warehouses for mid-century furniture and bizarre oddities.

todo.title: Crystal Palace Dinosaurs
todo.description: Created in 1854, these are the world's first dinosaur sculptures, delightfully historically inaccurate based on modern science.
todo.action: Wander the park's waterways to find these towering Victorian statues hidden in trees.
todo.photoTip: Eerie, overgrown Victorian dinosaur statues emerging from trees in the park.

todo.title: Sydenham Hill Wood
todo.description: A tract of ancient woodland inside the city, featuring the remains of an abandoned Victorian railway line.
todo.action: Take a tranquil walk through the dense canopy to find the abandoned railway tunnel.
todo.photoTip: Sweeping panoramic city views from the top of Crystal Palace hill.

todo.title: Horniman Museum & Gardens
todo.description: An eccentric Victorian museum in nearby Forest Hill famous for its oversized stuffed walrus, musical instruments, and botanical gardens.
todo.action: Visit the giant walrus in the natural history gallery and step into the 1897 Grade II listed conservatory.
todo.photoTip: The ornate Victorian ironwork conservatory overlooking panoramic vistas of the London skyline.

moreTodo.title: Crystal Palace Park Maze & Italian Terraces
moreTodo.description: One of the largest hedged mazes in the country dating to 1870, alongside the monumental surviving stone sphinxes and terraces of the burned-down Crystal Palace.
moreTodo.action: Navigate the dense yew labyrinth and inspect the giant stone sphinxes.
moreTodo.photoTip: The weathered stone sphinxes guarding the monumental stairs overlooking South London.

moreTodo.title: Dulwich Park & Boating Lake
moreTodo.description: A 72-acre Queen Anne style park created in 1890, famous for its springtime rhododendron and azalea walks and peaceful boating lake.
moreTodo.action: Hire a pedal boat or walk through the flowering American Garden.
moreTodo.photoTip: Vibrant rhododendrons reflecting across the tranquil waters of the duck pond.

eat.title: Megan's in the Hamlet
eat.description: Rustic, beautifully decorated Mediterranean spot in Dulwich Village.
eat.mustTry: Highly adaptable Mediterranean vegetarian dishes with great gluten-free options.

eat.title: Brown & Green Cafe Crystal Palace
eat.description: Bustling community cafe located right inside Crystal Palace Park.
eat.mustTry: Massive weekend brunch menu featuring abundant vegetarian and gluten-free choices.

name: Wimbledon & Putney 🎾
durationReason: A green and sporty single-day route seamlessly linking the historic hilltop Village, Wimbledon Common, and Putney's riverside rowing embankment.
season: Late June to early July. Buzzes with energy during Tennis Championships; pubs overflow with flowers.
transport: 🚇 District Line to Wimbledon or Putney Bridge.
funFacts: Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world, founded in 1877.
Wimbledon Common features an original 1817 windmill where Lord Baden-Powell wrote parts of 'Scouting for Boys'.
The Oxford vs Cambridge Boat Race starts its 4-mile course at Putney Bridge every spring.
soul: Leafy, sporty, and upper-crust. A stunning hilltop Village surrounded by massive commons, plus serene riverside rowing.

todo.title: Wimbledon Village
todo.description: Sitting on a hill, the 'Village' retains pristine 17th-century rural charm favored by affluent locals.
todo.action: Explore high-end boutiques and stop for a pint at a historic pub.
todo.photoTip: Historic, flower-draped pub facades in Wimbledon Village (Dog & Fox).

todo.title: Wimbledon Common & Windmill
todo.description: A 1,140-acre expanse of wild heathland, ponds, and woods, featuring a working windmill from 1817.
todo.action: Hike across the wilderness to find the isolated windmill museum.
todo.photoTip: Wimbledon Windmill standing isolated on the wild expanse of the Common.

todo.title: Putney Embankment
todo.description: The home of British rowing. This stretch of the Thames is lined with historic boat clubs and starts the Boat Race.
todo.action: Walk the Thames Path, watching rowing eights practice on the river.
todo.photoTip: Colorful rowing boats lined up along the Thames at Putney Embankment at sunset.

todo.title: Cannizaro Park
todo.description: A Grade II listed historic park situated behind a luxury hotel, renowned for ornamental landscaping.
todo.action: Visit the calm, beautiful walled gardens and the sunken garden.

todo.title: Wimbledon Lawn Tennis Museum & Tour
todo.description: The world's premier museum dedicated to lawn tennis, holding the championship trophies and Centre Court tour access.
todo.action: Tour Centre Court and view the historic Victorian tennis racquets.
todo.photoTip: The immaculate, striped grass court of Centre Court viewed from the Royal Box level.

moreTodo.title: Buddhapadipa Temple
moreTodo.description: The first Thai Buddhist temple built in the UK, an astonishing traditional gilded temple situated in 4 acres of quiet wooded meditation grounds.
moreTodo.action: Walk quietly around the ornate golden roof temple and cross the arched bridges over the fish ponds.
moreTodo.photoTip: The vibrant red and gold Thai temple architecture mirrored in the ornamental pond.

moreTodo.title: Fulham Palace & Walled Garden
moreTodo.description: Just across Putney Bridge, this historic manor was the countryside residence of the Bishops of London since 704 AD.
moreTodo.action: Explore the Tudor courtyard, Great Hall, and the restored Victorian vinery.
moreTodo.photoTip: The Tudor diaper-pattern brickwork courtyard and the blooming wisteria in the walled garden.

eat.title: Lu-Ma Cafe
eat.description: Health-focused independent cafe championing wellness and clean eating.
eat.mustTry: Dairy-free and meat-free menu with a huge focus on plant-based and gluten-free foods.

eat.title: The Ivy Cafe Wimbledon
eat.description: Sophisticated neighborhood brasserie in Wimbledon Village.
eat.mustTry: Dedicated vegetarian menu and a separate comprehensive gluten-free menu.

name: Walthamstow & The Wetlands 🦢
durationReason: An easy single day combining morning wetland walks across Europe's largest urban reservoir reserve with an afternoon of Arts & Crafts and neon art.
season: November. Early, dark evenings are perfect for God's Own Junkyard neon lights.
transport: 🚇 Victoria Line or Overground to Walthamstow Central or Blackhorse Road.
funFacts: Walthamstow Wetlands is Europe's largest urban wetland reserve, supplying water to millions.
William Morris, one of the most significant cultural figures of Victorian Britain, lived in Walthamstow.
God's Own Junkyard contains the oldest neon sign business in London and props from Hollywood movies.
soul: Rich Arts & Crafts history meets massive nature reserves and quirky, hyper-modern industrial art spaces.

todo.title: God's Own Junkyard
todo.description: A warehouse packed to the rafters with vintage neon signs, movie props, and disco balls salvaged over decades.
todo.action: Grab a drink at their cafe and be completely overwhelmed by the neon glow.
todo.photoTip: Sensory overload of neon lights inside God's Own Junkyard.

todo.title: Walthamstow Wetlands
todo.description: Europe's largest urban wetland reserve. A functioning water reservoir network that is a vital sanctuary for wildlife.
todo.action: Hike the pathways between reservoirs, looking out for the Victorian Engine House.
todo.photoTip: The Engine House at Wetlands, with its Victorian chimney reflected in water.

todo.title: William Morris Gallery
todo.description: Set in the 18th-century Georgian house where the famous Arts and Crafts pioneer lived, showcasing his intricate textiles and wallpapers.
todo.action: Admire the revolutionary floral prints and original weaving looms on display.
todo.photoTip: Intricate Arts and Crafts wallpaper patterns preserved inside William Morris Gallery.

todo.title: Walthamstow Village (Orford Road)
todo.description: A pedestrianized pocket of E17 that retains a deeply historic, village feel with independent shops and delis.
todo.action: Stroll down Orford Road, popping into independent delis and cafes.

todo.title: Blackhorse Beer Mile & Taprooms
todo.description: A dynamic industrial strip of independent breweries and creative studios hosting street food pop-ups.
todo.action: Walk from Blackhorse Road station to explore the artisan spaces and outdoor seating.
todo.photoTip: Bold murals on industrial brick walls along the Blackhorse creative path.

moreTodo.title: Vestry House Museum
moreTodo.description: Built in 1730 as a parish workhouse, now exploring local domestic history, housing the 1892 Bremer car (the first British four-wheeled petrol car).
moreTodo.action: Walk through the restored Victorian workhouse garden planted with historic dye and medicinal herbs.
moreTodo.photoTip: The idyllic brick workhouse facade framed by lush cottage garden flowers.

moreTodo.title: Walthamstow Town Hall & Civic Water Fountains
moreTodo.description: A striking 1941 Portland stone Nordic-classicist Art Deco civic palace with monumental relief sculptures and a massive reflecting pool.
moreTodo.action: Watch the evening fountain light display dancing across the water courtyard.
moreTodo.photoTip: The white Portland stone clock tower and classical statues reflected symmetrically in the pool.

eat.title: Wood St Coffee
eat.description: Independent specialty coffee shop and brunch spot near Blackhorse Road.
eat.mustTry: Excellent vegetarian brunch dishes with easy gluten-free bread swaps.

eat.title: The Bell Walthamstow
eat.description: Massive community gastropub anchored in the heart of E17.
eat.mustTry: Fantastic Sunday roasts with dedicated vegan and gluten-free alternatives.
